dedupe_keys.name: surrogate fuel compositions and energy recovery estimates for 30 incinerated norwegian waste classes

description: This database describes the fuel that Norwegian waste-to-energy plants burn, by reducing each common waste class to a handful of representative chemical compounds whose heating value and emissions can be modelled. The producers are Ivar Tustervatn Berre, Candy Anquetil-Deck and Corinna Schulze-Netzer of the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, from a 2023 thesis on energy recovery and emission potential. Coverage is 41 waste components combined into surrogate formulations for 30 waste classes typically incinerated in Norway, together with estimates of higher heating value and the shares of biogenic, fossil oil-based and inorganic material, and statistics comparing model and experimental values. Python scripts for the fitting are included, and both archives are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: thesis-level work, surrogates depend on literature composition data, and the classes follow Norwegian waste categories. Simulation uses: modelling the variable feedstock of incineration plants, estimating heat and electricity output for district heating, and the fossil carbon share for emission accounting. Related records: the China incineration monitoring data (data-china-msw-incineration-monitoring) track plant emissions in operation.
